chief_complaint: recurrent sudden episodes of severe lip swelling and abdominal cramps without itchy hives
hpi_details: 32F with family history presenting with non-pruritic, non-urticarial lip/hand swelling and colicky abdominal pain. Low C4 and C1 esterase inhibitor levels; unresponsive to antihistamines/epinephrine.
ideas: She thinks she might have developed a severe allergy to a cosmetic product or food additive that regular allergy pills cannot touch, similar to the mysterious swelling episodes her mother used to experience.
concerns: She is worried that the swelling will spread to her throat and suffocate her while she is home alone.
expectations: She hopes to leave with a stronger rescue shot or targeted prescription medicine to halt the swelling immediately when an attack starts.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Hereditary Angioedema (C1-inhibitor deficiency) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Hereditary Angioedema (C1-inhibitor deficiency) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management is bradykinin-targeted (e.g., C1 inhibitor concentrate, icatibant, or ecallantide) rather than antihistamines, epinephrine, or corticosteroids, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: recurrent sudden episodes of severe lip swelling and abdominal cramps without itchy hives

Key HPI features: 32F with family history presenting with non-pruritic, non-urticarial lip/hand swelling and colicky abdominal pain. Low C4 and C1 esterase inhibitor levels; unresponsive to antihistamines/epinephrine.
Objective/Exam findings: Non-pitting, non-pruritic edema of the lips and hand without urticarial wheals; low C4 with low C1 esterase inhibitor antigenic and functional levels.
Relevant background/PMH: No significant chronic medical history
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Hereditary Angioedema (C1-inhibitor deficiency).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Allergic angioedema without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Laryngeal swelling with voice change or stridor.
management_principles: Treat attacks early — especially any laryngeal involvement — with an on-demand bradykinin-targeted therapy (IV C1 inhibitor concentrate, icatibant, or ecallantide) rather than antihistamines or epinephrine
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Hereditary Angioedema C1 Inhibitor Deficiency: recurrent sudden episodes of severe lip swelling and abdominal cramps without itchy hives. 32F with family history presenting with non-pruritic, non-urticarial lip/hand swelling and colicky abdominal pain. Low C4 and C1 esterase inhibitor levels; unresponsive to antihistamines/epinephrine.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals normal between attacks. Non-pitting, non-pruritic edema of the lips and hand without urticarial wheals. Complement C4 low; C1 esterase inhibitor quantitative antigen and functional activity both low.
reference_soap.assessment: Hereditary Angioedema (HAE) Type 1 secondary to C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Treat attacks early with an on-demand bradykinin-targeted therapy (IV C1 inhibitor concentrate, icatibant, or ecallantide); treat any laryngeal involvement as an airway emergency and prepare for emergency airway management if respiratory compromise progresses. 2. Antihistamines, epinephrine, and corticosteroids do not target bradykinin-mediated HAE and should not delay HAE-specific therapy. 3. Refer to an allergy/immunology specialist for confirmatory testing, individualized long-term prophylaxis, and an emergency action plan.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features and diagnostic criteria of Hereditary Angioedema C1 Inhibitor Deficiency
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for recurrent sudden episodes of severe lip swelling and abdominal cramps without itchy hives
Select appropriate laboratory and imaging studies for allergy_immunology
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies

teaching.one_liner: Recurrent bradykinin-mediated swelling from low or dysfunctional C1-esterase inhibitor — supported by low C4 plus abnormal C1-INH antigenic and functional testing, not by allergy testing.
red_flags: Laryngeal swelling with voice change or stridor
Severe abdominal attack mimicking an acute abdomen

must_ask.say: Is the swelling itchy, or does it come without any itching or hives?
Does anything seem to set off an episode — stress, minor injury, dental work?
Do you ever get severe abdominal pain with the swelling?
Does this run in your family?
Have antihistamines or epinephrine ever helped?

history.answer: My lips swelled up huge out of nowhere this morning, and now I'm having severe cramping stomach pain.
Right now it's my upper and lower lips that are swollen, and my right hand is puffy too. My legs, feet, and eyes aren't swollen at all.
The swelling came on suddenly around breakfast time and expanded over a couple of hours. The severe belly cramps started shortly afterwards.
No, it doesn't change between morning and evening. Once an attack starts, it just stays swollen for two or three days before gradually fading.
When I press on my lip or hand, it feels firm and doesn't leave any dent. My wedding ring did get stuck because of the hand puffiness, though.
No, my weight has been completely stable.
No, neither leg hurts, and there is no redness or hot feeling anywhere on my legs.
I'm breathing fine right now and I have no trouble lying flat in bed. I'm just terrified that my throat might start swelling next.
My throat feels clear and my voice sounds normal right now. I don't have any raspy breathing or trouble swallowing today.
No, my urine is completely clear and light yellow with no bubbles or dark cola color, and I go a normal amount.
My stomach feels bloated from the cramps, but my skin and eyes are not yellow, and I don't bruise or bleed easily.
It's a severe, colicky cramping all across my belly that comes in waves, and I feel quite nauseated. I've had these sudden stomach attacks a few times before.
No, I haven't had a sore throat, runny nose, or skin infection recently.
No, I don't feel unusually cold, I don't have constipation, and my skin isn't abnormally dry.
I can't eat anything today because my stomach hurts so much, but I haven't had chronic diarrhea or unintentional weight loss.
No, I haven't had any surgery, I haven't taken any long flights, and I haven't been bedridden or diagnosed with cancer.
I don't take any blood pressure medications like amlodipine, nor do I take ACE inhibitors, painkillers, steroids, or hormone pills.
I don't eat salty food often, and while I sit at a desk for work, my feet never swell up at the end of the day.
There is absolutely no itching and no red hives or welts anywhere. It's just deep, tight swelling.
I've been under a lot of stress at work this week, and I accidentally bit my lower lip yesterday. Minor bumps or dental procedures seem to trigger these episodes.
During my last bad flare, the emergency doctors gave me antihistamine pills, steroid injections, and even an epinephrine shot, but none of them did anything.
I don't have any chronic medical illnesses like high blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, or kidney problems.
I've been getting these random swelling episodes in my hands, feet, or lips along with bad stomach cramps about three or four times a year since I was a teenager.
I've gone to the emergency room for severe belly cramps before, but I've never had any surgeries or hospital admissions.
I am not taking any prescription medications, herbal products, or supplements.
I have no allergies to medications, foods, or bee stings.
My mother and my maternal uncle both have a history of repeated unexplained swelling and severe belly pain attacks.
My last period started two weeks ago and my cycles are very regular every 28 days. I'm not pregnant, and my husband and I use condoms.
I have never smoked cigarettes. I only have one or two glasses of wine socially on weekends.
I work full-time as an accountant in an office and live at home with my husband.
I'm terrified that the swelling will hit my throat next and choke me before anyone can get here to help.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert and in mild discomfort due to facial swelling and abdominal cramps, with no acute respiratory distress or stridor.
Marked non-erythematous, non-pitting edema of the upper and lower lips; tongue, uvula, and posterior pharynx show normal caliber without mucosal swelling or airway compromise.
Bilateral breath sounds are clear to auscultation without wheezing, crackles, or stridor.
Regular rhythm and rate with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or third heart sound.
Slightly full abdomen without visible distension, caput medusae, or spider angiomas.
Hyperactive, colicky bowel sounds audible throughout all four abdominal quadrants.
Diffuse mild tenderness on deep palpation throughout the abdomen without voluntary guarding or muscular rigidity.
No rebound tenderness elicited in any abdominal quadrant.
Percussion is diffusely tympanitic with no shifting dullness or detectable fluid wave.
Firm, non-pitting edema noted over the right dorsal hand and fingers; no pretibial pitting edema on either lower extremity.
Both calves are symmetric in circumference without localized warmth, erythema, cords, or tenderness.
Localized non-pitting, non-pruritic swelling of the lips and right hand without urticarial plaques, wheals, or icterus.
Thyroid is normal in size, non-tender, and smooth without palpable nodules or bruits.
No jugular venous distension; jugular venous pulsation is normal below the clavicular margin at 45 degrees.
